entities_included.other: Consolidated statements (Note 1, PDF p.21, printed p.20) cover Harvard Management Company (wholly owned subsidiary), the Faculty of Arts and Sciences, SEAS, the Division of Continuing Education (Harvard Extension School), ten graduate and professional Schools, Radcliffe, museums and the library system. No teaching hospital is consolidated: the report refers to the 'Harvard-affiliated teaching hospitals' as separate organizations (PDF p.23). Sponsored support revenue is $973M in FY25.

calibration_fy23.explanation: Original slide S&W ($2,421,076,000) equals the audited FY23 'Salaries and wages' line to the dollar (0.0%). Original 'core operating expenses' ($5,911,797,000) equals audited FY23 TOTAL operating expenses to the dollar; on the stated definition (less depreciation $424.8M and interest $208.6M) FY23 core is $5,278,398,000, so the original x value was 12.0% too high. Same finding as for the other schools. Original student count 21,400 = the report's 'approximately 7,200 undergraduate and 14,200 graduate students in fiscal year 2023' (Note 1, PDF p.22).

student_counts_in_official_docs: FY25 Financial Report, Note 1, PDF p.21 (printed p.20): 'approximately 7,000 undergraduate and 14,000 graduate students in fiscal year 2025, as compared to 7,100 undergraduate and 13,900 graduate students in fiscal year 2024' = about 21,000 in each year; consistent with the CDS 2024-25 grand total of 21,189 used on the slide. FY23 report, Note 1, PDF p.22 (printed p.21): 'approximately 7,200 undergraduate and 14,200 graduate students in fiscal year 2023, as compared to 7,100 undergraduate and 14,100 graduate students in fiscal year 2022' (the original slide's 21,400).
caveats: Provided by the user, not downloaded: finance.harvard.edu returns Akamai 403 to non-browser clients, so the audited PDF was supplied by Brett. All figures were read from that PDF (pdftotext -layout) and tie: the nine natural-classification lines sum to total operating expenses in both years ($6,794,371K FY25; $6,426,911K FY24).

Students: the slide uses the Common Data Set fall 2024 total (21,189, degree schools only) PLUS Harvard Extension School degree students in fall 2024 (621 undergraduate + 3,009 graduate = 3,630, Harvard OIRA Fact Book 2025-26, historical headcount table, 'As of October 15 of the academic year') = 24,819, because the expenses include the Division of Continuing Education. Alternatives: Fact Book University total degree headcount 24,519 (distinct students); IPEDS fall 2023 total 30,386 (adds non-degree Extension students). See the S3_Sensitivity sheet, section E.
Harvard's S&W and benefits lines are clean, separate lines (benefits are 27.4% of S&W in FY25, 26.2% in FY24), so no assumed fringe rate is needed.

Interest ($262.5M) and depreciation ($459.0M) are separate operating lines; 'Fixed asset impairments' ($20.9M FY25) sit inside Other expenses and are NOT removed (the definition removes only depreciation, amortization and interest).
Harvard's total operating expenses are before non-operating items; the FY25 operating deficit is $112.6M (general operating account basis).
